ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A 50 kg passenger takes an elevator which, at t=0, starts from rest on the ground and rises to the top floor in 10 s. The graph of the elevator's acceleration as a function of time is as shown in the figure, where a positive value of acceleration indicates an upward direction, and take g as 10 \mathrm{m/s^{2}}. According to the graph, what is the minimum magnitude of the force exerted by the passenger on the floor?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The minimum magnitude of the force exerted by the passenger on the floor is 350 N
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: The figure is a graph of the elevator acceleration a changing with time t; the unit of the vertical axis is m·s^-2, and the positive direction indicates upward. The front section of the curve has upward positive acceleration, and the rear section has downward negative acceleration; from the graph it can be read that the minimum value of the acceleration is about a_min=-3 m/s^2. Then reason: The passenger's mass m=50 kg, and take upward as the positive direction. The forces on the passenger are the floor's supporting force N upward and gravity mg downward; therefore, applying Newton's second law to the passenger: N-mg=ma, giving N=m(g+a). The force exerted by the passenger on the floor is equal in magnitude to the supporting force exerted by the floor on the passenger, so to find the minimum force exerted by the passenger on the floor is to find the minimum value of N. Since N=m(g+a), N is minimum when a is minimum. Substitute a_min=-3 m/s^2 and g=10 m/s^2: N_min=50×(10-3)=350 N.
